dialogue.origin: こんばんは！今日はよろしくお願いします！19:00にまたご連絡しますね！
dialogue.content: Good evening! I look forward to our session today. I will contact you again at 7:00 PM!

dialogue.origin: よろしくお願いします！
dialogue.content: I look forward to it, thank you!

dialogue.origin: こんばんは、相談員です。今日はどのようなご相談ですか？
dialogue.content: Good evening, I'm the counselor. What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.origin: 仕事辞めたいなと考えています
dialogue.content: I'm thinking about quitting my job.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね。もう少し詳しく教えていただけますか？
dialogue.content: I see. Could you tell me a bit more about that?

dialogue.origin: 社長がなんでもかんでも怒鳴るんです
dialogue.content: The president yells at me for every little thing.

dialogue.origin: それはおつらいですね・・・
dialogue.content: That must be very difficult for you...

dialogue.origin: もうビクビクして落ち着かない
dialogue.content: I'm constantly on edge and can't relax.

dialogue.origin: なるほどですね。
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: どんなことを言われるのですか？
dialogue.content: What kinds of things does he say to you?

dialogue.origin: ハンコの位置がずれているとか
dialogue.content: Things like, 'The placement of the stamp is off.'

dialogue.origin: けど5ミリくらいなんです
dialogue.content: But it's only off by about 5 millimeters.

dialogue.origin: 電話で少々お待ちくださいと先方に伝えてるところを聞かれて
dialogue.content: He overheard me telling someone on the phone, "Please hold for a moment," and...

dialogue.origin: そう細かい指示を受けると、参ってしまいますよね・・・
dialogue.content: Getting such nitpicky instructions can really wear you down...

dialogue.origin: ええ、続けてください
dialogue.content: Yes, please go on.

dialogue.origin: 少々はすぐのことだから
dialogue.content: He said that "a moment" means immediately,

dialogue.origin: すぐ返答しなきゃ失礼だ！とかほんとう細かいというか八つ当たりなんです
dialogue.content: and that I have to respond immediately or it's rude! It's so nitpicky, or rather, he's just taking it out on us.

dialogue.origin: 前の日は右に押せと言われたハンコを次の日はなんで右に押してるんだ左だろ！とか
dialogue.content: For instance, one day he'll tell me to put the stamp on the right, and the next day he's yelling, "Why did you stamp it on the right? It's supposed to be on the left!"

dialogue.origin: 私たちに非がないことばかり
dialogue.content: It's always for things that aren't our fault.

dialogue.origin: そんなことまで言われているのですね・・・
dialogue.content: He even says things like that to you...

dialogue.origin: 落ち着いて仕事もできなくなりますよね
dialogue.content: It must make it impossible to focus on your work, doesn't it?

dialogue.origin: 間違えちゃいけない、怒らせちゃいけないすごい緊張感です
dialogue.content: There's this incredible tension of, "I can't make a mistake, I can't make him angry."

dialogue.origin: なるほどですね。おつらいですね・・・他にお仕事辞めたい理由はありますか？
dialogue.content: I see. That sounds very painful... Are there any other reasons you want to quit?

dialogue.origin: 他の職員は良い人ばかりで
dialogue.content: Everyone else at work is nice, though.

dialogue.origin: 給料も悪くないしまあこれは高くして社長のことを我慢させてるのかなと今なら思うんですけど、、、
dialogue.content: And the pay isn't bad either... though now I wonder if he's paying us well just to make us put up with him...

dialogue.origin: 同僚の方がいい人なのは、すばらしいことですね。
dialogue.content: It's wonderful that your coworkers are good people.

dialogue.origin: けどだからこそ誰かが社長を怒らせるとみんなに迷惑かけるから
dialogue.content: But that's exactly why if someone angers the president, it causes trouble for everyone,

dialogue.origin: 申し訳なくて、、、
dialogue.content: and I feel so sorry about that...

dialogue.origin: そうなのですね。
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: では、社長の指示が細かくてストレスを感じられていて、
dialogue.content: So, you're feeling stressed because of the president's nitpicky instructions,

dialogue.origin: なおかつ同僚の方にも怒らせることで迷惑をかけてしまうのではないかと思って、
dialogue.content: and on top of that, you're worried about causing trouble for your colleagues by making him angry,

dialogue.origin: お仕事を辞めたいと考えられているのですね。
dialogue.content: and that's why you're thinking about quitting your job.

dialogue.origin: 理不尽な八つ当たりにストレスが感じられます原因は私たちじゃないんです
dialogue.content: The stress comes from his unreasonable venting, and it's not our fault.

dialogue.origin: 昨日のゴルフのスコアが悪かったとか
dialogue.content: Like his golf score was bad yesterday,

dialogue.origin: 子どもが入試に失敗したとか
dialogue.content: or his child failed an entrance exam.

dialogue.origin: 社長さんの一方的な態度が原因ということですね。
dialogue.content: So the cause is the president's one-sided behavior.

dialogue.origin: そういうことまで言われると、苦しくなるのもわかります・・・
dialogue.content: Hearing things like that, I can understand why you feel so distressed...

dialogue.origin: お仕事をお辞めになりたいのは、もう決断されているのですか？
dialogue.content: Have you already decided that you want to quit?

dialogue.origin: そうなんです怒鳴ってストレス発散したいがために粗探しして私たちが苦しめられているんです
dialogue.content: That's right. He's just looking for faults so he can yell and relieve his stress, and we're the ones who suffer.

dialogue.origin: 職員は順々に辞めていますが、、、辞める話し合いをするのも大変で
dialogue.content: Staff members have been quitting one after another... but it's very difficult just to have the conversation about quitting.

dialogue.origin: 他の方も、やめられているのですね・・・
dialogue.content: So other people have been quitting as well...

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: また怒鳴られるのも怖くて
dialogue.content: I'm scared of being yelled at again.

dialogue.origin: そうですよね
dialogue.content: That's understandable.

dialogue.origin: ではすでにお仕事はお辞めになりたいとは思っていて、
dialogue.content: So, you already feel you want to quit your job,

dialogue.origin: 今までは我慢できていたんですが最近ついに職場で泣いてしまいました
dialogue.content: I've been able to endure it until now, but recently I finally broke down and cried at work.

dialogue.origin: 辞めるにも社長に伝えるのが怖い、とお悩みなのですね。
dialogue.content: but you're struggling with the fear of telling the president you want to quit. Is that the issue?

dialogue.origin: 伝えてから実際やめるまでもう存在を無視される扱いをされるんです
dialogue.content: After you tell him, until the day you actually leave, he gives you the silent treatment, as if you don't exist.

dialogue.origin: そうだったのですね・・・それは、本当につらかったのですね・・・
dialogue.content: I see... That must have been truly painful...

dialogue.origin: はい…
dialogue.content: Yes...

dialogue.origin: では、一緒にどうやったら、社長さんに辞めたいと伝えられるか、
dialogue.content: Then, let's think together about how you can tell the president you want to quit,

dialogue.origin: 一緒に考えていきましょう。
dialogue.content: and let's figure it out together.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Okay.

dialogue.origin: 社長さんの態度に違和感を感じたのは、いつごろからですか？
dialogue.content: When did you first start feeling that something was off about the president's behavior?

dialogue.origin: 入社してすぐでした
dialogue.content: It was right after I joined the company.

dialogue.origin: 面接の時は愛想が良くてわからなかったんです
dialogue.content: He was so pleasant during the interview, I had no idea.

dialogue.origin: もう入社して初めから感じられていたのですね。
dialogue.content: So you felt that way from the very beginning after joining.

dialogue.origin: けど辞めるにしてもまだこの職場に8ヶ月しかいないんです
dialogue.content: But even if I quit, I've only been at this company for eight months.

dialogue.origin: 何年ぐらい働かれているんですか？
dialogue.content: How many years have you been working there?

dialogue.origin: 行き違い、失礼しました
dialogue.content: Oh, we cross-posted. My apologies.

dialogue.origin: いえ一年たってないので転職も不利になるんじゃないかと不安です
dialogue.content: No, it's fine. Since it hasn't even been a year, I'm worried it will be a disadvantage when I look for a new job.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、そうなのですね。そうお感じになられるのも当然だと思います。
dialogue.content: I see, so that's your concern. It's completely understandable that you would feel that way.

dialogue.origin: けどもう行くのも辛くて毎朝吐き気がして…実際吐いてしまう日もあって…
dialogue.content: But it's gotten so hard to go to work that I feel nauseous every morning... and some days I actually throw up...

dialogue.origin: なんと、そんなこともあったのですね・・・
dialogue.content: My goodness, that's been happening...?

dialogue.origin: 他の同僚の方も順々に辞められているとおっしゃっていましたが、
dialogue.content: You mentioned that your other colleagues have also been quitting one after another,

dialogue.origin: 自分でも限界なんじゃないかと思ってます
dialogue.content: I think I might be at my limit myself.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 何かお話とか聞いていますか？
dialogue.content: Have you heard anything about their situations?

dialogue.origin: みんなも限界だって
dialogue.content: That everyone else was at their limit too.

dialogue.origin: 今のお話を伺うと、それもうなずけます・・・
dialogue.content: Hearing your story, I can certainly see why...

dialogue.origin: 実際辞められた方は、その後どうされているのですか？
dialogue.content: What have the people who actually quit been doing since they left?

dialogue.origin: その後とは？
dialogue.content: By "afterward," what do you mean?

dialogue.origin: 他の仕事してるか？とかですか？
dialogue.content: Like, if they've found other jobs?

dialogue.origin: 先ほど転職にも不安があるとのことだったので、
dialogue.content: Since you mentioned earlier that you're anxious about changing jobs,

dialogue.origin: 他の方はどうされているのかと思いまして。
dialogue.content: I was wondering what the others have been doing.

dialogue.origin: そうですね…なんだかんだお仕事してると聞いていますあとは結婚とか子育てとか
dialogue.content: Right... I hear they've all managed to find work. Others have gotten married or are raising children.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、そうなのですね。それを聞いて、何か感じたこととかはありましたか？
dialogue.content: I see. How did you feel when you heard that?

dialogue.origin: あーいいなって
dialogue.content: I thought, 'That sounds nice.'

dialogue.origin: そう感じますよね。
dialogue.content: It's natural to feel that way.

dialogue.origin: うらやましいですよね
dialogue.content: It makes you feel envious, doesn't it?

dialogue.origin: なので、一歩進むためのお手伝いをしたいです
dialogue.content: That's why I want to help you take that next step forward.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 転職をするうえで、経歴がどうしても不利になってしまうとのことでしたが、
dialogue.content: You mentioned that your short tenure might be a disadvantage for job hunting,

dialogue.origin: その他に、転職する上で不安なことはありますか？
dialogue.content: Are there any other concerns you have about changing jobs?

dialogue.origin: 転職活動の方はないですとにかく辞めにくいということだけです…
dialogue.content: Not about the job search itself. It's really just that it's so hard to quit...

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます。それに尽きるのですね。
dialogue.content: Thank you. So it all comes down to that.

dialogue.origin: 実際辞められた同僚の方は、どうようにして辞めることができたのですか？
dialogue.content: How did the colleagues who quit manage to do so?

dialogue.origin: ↑どのように
dialogue.content: —sorry, I meant, in what way?

dialogue.origin: 半数がケンカ別れですね残りは結婚、出産、旦那さんの転勤とかの理由で辞めてます
dialogue.content: About half left on bad terms. The rest quit for reasons like marriage, childbirth, or their husband's job transfer.

dialogue.origin: 残りのほうがまだ穏便に辞めれています
dialogue.content: The latter group was able to leave more amicably.

dialogue.origin: では、何かしら正当な理由があれば、受け入れてはもらえるのですね。
dialogue.content: So, if there's some kind of legitimate reason, he does accept it.

dialogue.origin: そうですね…不機嫌にはなりますけど仕方がないから受け入れてますね
dialogue.content: Yes... he gets moody about it, but he accepts it because he has no choice.

dialogue.origin: 不機嫌になるのは、不安に感じるかもしれないですが、
dialogue.content: He might get moody, which could make you feel anxious, but

dialogue.origin: 辞めるのを伝えるのは最善かもしれないですね。
dialogue.content: telling him you're quitting might be the best course of action.

dialogue.origin: 社長さんが断りにくい理由をつくる、それを考えるのも一つの方法かもしれません。
dialogue.content: Thinking of a reason that's hard for the president to refuse could be one approach.

dialogue.origin: 社長が不機嫌になっても辞めたいというしかないってことですよね
dialogue.content: So you're saying I just have to tell him I want to quit, even if he gets upset.

dialogue.origin: 断りにくい理由か
dialogue.content: A reason that's hard to refuse, huh.

dialogue.origin: 差し支えなければ、どのようにお呼びすればいいか教えていただけませんか？
dialogue.content: If you don't mind, could you tell me what I should call you?

dialogue.origin: ピーです
dialogue.content: It's P.

dialogue.origin: ピーさんですね。ありがとうございます。
dialogue.content: Okay, P. Thank you.

dialogue.origin: 例えば、家族の世話をするために長期間お仕事を休まなければいけないとか、
dialogue.content: For example, saying you need to take a long leave of absence to care for a family member,

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 身体が病気がちで、長期休養を取らなければいけなくなったとか、
dialogue.content: or that you've been unwell and need to take an extended rest,

dialogue.origin: 社長が断ることが倫理的に良くないことを理由にするのも手だと思います。
dialogue.content: Using a reason that would be ethically wrong for the president to refuse is one option.

dialogue.origin: 特にピーさんは、やめたい理由の中に、同僚に迷惑をかけたくないとおっしゃていて、
dialogue.content: Especially since you, P, mentioned that one of the reasons you're hesitant to quit is not wanting to trouble your colleagues,

dialogue.origin: なるほどたしかにそういった理由なら社長が断ると問題が発生しますね
dialogue.content: I see. It's true that if I gave a reason like that, it would cause a problem if the president refused.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 自分が苦しいのに、周りの人のことを考えられていて、
dialogue.content: Even though you're suffering yourself, you're still thinking about the people around you,

dialogue.origin: とてもお優しい方と感じました。
dialogue.content: which makes me feel that you are a very kind person.

dialogue.origin: ただ周りのことを考えるあまり、自分を犠牲にしてしまって、
dialogue.content: However, by thinking so much about others, you might be sacrificing yourself,

dialogue.origin: 自分を追い詰めてしまい苦しくなることもあるとは思います。
dialogue.content: and I think that can sometimes back you into a corner and cause you pain.

dialogue.origin: だからこそ周りに迷惑をかけない穏便な方法で、
dialogue.content: That's why finding a peaceful method that won't cause trouble for others,

dialogue.origin: なおかつ自分をいたわるためにも、
dialogue.content: and also allows you to take care of yourself,

dialogue.origin: 私は社長が受け入れやすい理由を作るのがいいと思いましたよ。
dialogue.content: is why I thought creating a reason the president can easily accept would be a good idea.

dialogue.origin: 今の話を聴いて、どう感じましたか？
dialogue.content: How do you feel after hearing that?

dialogue.origin: そうですね…周りも自分も傷つけない
dialogue.content: You're right... it wouldn't hurt those around me, or myself.

dialogue.origin: なるべく穏便にすむのは理想です
dialogue.content: It's ideal to resolve it as peacefully as possible.

dialogue.origin: 理由を見つけるのは、もしかしたら難しいかもしれないですが、
dialogue.content: Finding a reason might be difficult, but

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: 8か月間必死で働いてこられたピーさんなら、
dialogue.content: for you, P, who has worked so hard for these eight months,

dialogue.origin: きっと見つけられます。
dialogue.content: I'm sure you can find one.

dialogue.origin: そしてこの8か月間、
dialogue.content: And for these past eight months,

dialogue.origin: よく頑張ってこられましたね。
dialogue.content: you have done so well to endure.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます
dialogue.content: Thank you.

dialogue.origin: 理由考えてみます
dialogue.content: I'll try to think of a reason.

dialogue.origin: ここまでお話を聴いて、どう感じたか、教えていただけますか？
dialogue.content: Could you tell me how you feel after our conversation so far?

dialogue.origin: ぜひ、考えてみてください。
dialogue.content: Please do give it some thought.

dialogue.origin: 周りにも迷惑かけたくなくてどうしていいかわからなかったけど
dialogue.content: I didn't want to cause trouble for others, so I didn't know what to do, but

dialogue.origin: きっと見つかります。
dialogue.content: I'm sure you'll find one.

dialogue.origin: はい、聴いているので続けてください
dialogue.content: Yes, I'm listening, please continue.

dialogue.origin: 我慢しなくていいかな
dialogue.content: maybe it's okay for me to stop enduring this.

dialogue.origin: なるべく穏便に理由つけて辞めれたら我慢も辞めるまでですものね
dialogue.content: If I can quit peacefully with a good reason, then I only have to endure it until I leave, right?

dialogue.origin: いいですね、周りも自分も大切にしましょう
dialogue.content: That's a great way to think about it. Let's value both others and yourself.

dialogue.origin: はいそうします
dialogue.content: Yes, I will.

dialogue.origin: そうですね。その方が、お互いにとって良いようにも思います。
dialogue.content: Yes. I think that would be better for everyone involved.

dialogue.origin: では、相談の方を終了しますね。
dialogue.content: Well then, we'll bring this session to a close.

dialogue.origin: はい、ありがとうございました
dialogue.content: Yes, thank you very much.

topic.sub: 社長の理不尽な指示によるストレス
